- When sentiment is consistently negative (last 3–5 days < -0.30), model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–2% relative to prior peak.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., +5%+ in 3–5 days), model often overshoots; cap forecast at +3–5% above recent high, then allow gradual decay.
- If sentiment turns positive after a downtrend (e.g., last 3 days > 0.10), model underreacts; increase forecast by 0.5–1.5% per positive sentiment day.
- Mean reversion bias: if forecast is >10% above 30-day moving average, reduce by 1–2% per day until convergence.
- For 30-day horizon, model often overweights recent volatility; smooth forecast by averaging last 7–10 days’ values before applying sentiment adjustment.
- If sentiment is neutral or mildly negative (0.0–-0.20), model tends to lag; add 0.5–1.0% to forecast to compensate for delayed reaction.
